source.reuse_scope: Algorithm description only; ports, workload, oracles, and prose are clean-room.

contract.operation: Maintain a sequence as maximal constant-value intervals and process range assignment, range addition, kth-order-statistic, and modular power-sum operations.
contract.input_layout: [N,Q,initial_values..., variable-width operations...]; assignment/add/kth records are [kind,left,right,arg], power-sum records are [3,left,right,exponent,modulus].
contract.indexing: All update and query ranges are zero-based and inclusive.
contract.kth_rank: For opcode 2, arg is a one-based rank within the queried range.
contract.power_sum: Opcode 3 uses exponent 0..8 and modulus 1..1000000000; 0^0 is defined as 1 before reduction.

opcodes.0: assign each value in [left,right] to arg
opcodes.1: add arg to each value in [left,right]
opcodes.2: return the arg-th smallest value in [left,right]
opcodes.3: return sum(value^exponent mod modulus) mod modulus over [left,right]

contract.algorithm: Store ordered, non-overlapping maximal equal-value intervals. Split at right+1 before left, replace or update the covered interval records, then coalesce equal neighbors. Kth queries expand intersecting runs and sort the bounded values; power sums multiply each run's modular power by its overlap width.
contract.output_layout: One little-endian signed 64-bit answer for each opcode 2 or 3, in operation order.
contract.error_policy: Malformed input returns -1. If at least one answer is produced, a null output pointer or capacity below 8*answer_count returns -2 without writes. When there are no answers, a null output pointer is accepted and success returns 0.
contract.complexity: With R current runs and at most N array elements, the sorted-array ordered set uses O(R) boundary lookup/insertion/deletion; an update is O(R), kth is O(R+N^2) in the insertion-sort ports, and power-sum is O(R log exponent). The randomized-like assignment traces tend to merge runs, but there is no worst-case guarantee: singleton assignments can maintain Θ(N) runs, giving construction-sensitive Θ(NQ) update and power-sum scanning (plus kth sorting). Storage is O(N+Q).
